## HueMux v0.0.5-alpha.5 — Connections that died without saying so

> **Alpha.** Built and tested in CI. This one fixes a failure that made the
> app look broken after a laptop slept: the panel stopped following the lamps
> while its connection indicator stayed green.
>
> It is the same change as `v0.0.5-alpha.4`, which published nothing: two
> unchecked `SetReadDeadline` calls in the new test file failed the lint job, so
> the release workflow stopped before building anything.

### The bug

Recall a scene from the Hue app, from the wall panel, or from anywhere else,
and the lamps moved — but the lights page did not follow. The cards kept the
colours and levels they had. Nothing was wrong with the scene path: the bridge
reported the change and the service forwarded it. It was arriving on a socket
that was already dead.

A WebSocket dies without a close frame when the machine it belongs to sleeps,
changes network, or has its process killed. There is no FIN, so neither side is
told: `readyState` stays 1, `onclose` never runs, writes are accepted into a
kernel buffer nobody will read, and every message after that moment is lost.
The page went on rendering the last state it knew, with a working-looking
connection dot, and the only visible symptom was that it had stopped tracking.
On the service side the same socket stayed in the broadcast set forever.

### What changed

Silence is now treated as death on both sides, because it is the only evidence
either side can get.

**The page recovers on its own.** Every page's socket is now watched by
`web/shared/ws-liveness.js`. The service pushes a status snapshot once a
second, so a healthy connection is never quiet; 15 seconds of silence — fifteen
missed pushes — is a dead socket, and the page closes it and reconnects. The
service sends a full snapshot to every client the moment it connects, so the
reconnect is also the resync. Returning to a tab rechecks the same clock, which
is what covers the laptop that slept with the tab open: a socket that went
quiet while the screen was off gets a real reconnect instead of a message sent
into the void.

**The service reaps them.** The same status loop now sends a ping every 10
seconds and closes any connection that has sent nothing back for 35 seconds —
counting the automatic pong a browser returns with no page code involved, so an
idle tab is never mistaken for a dead one. That close ends the connection's
read loop, removes it from the broadcast set, and gives a `close` event even to
an older client that has no watchdog of its own.

Verified against the running instance: a peer that never answers is dropped at
35 seconds, and one that answers every ping is still connected at 46.

### Updating

The Android app bundles the frontend, so **take the APK from this release** —
the page-side watchdog is not in the previous one. A desktop browser only needs
a reload. The service-side half reaches every already-installed client as soon
as this version is running, including the old APK, which is what turns its
zombie connection into an ordinary close it can already recover from.
